Nŏmĭus and Nŏmĭos , ii, and Nŏ-mĭon , ōnis, m., = Νόμιος and Νομίων,
I.the Pasturer, a surname of Apollo, because he tended the flocks of Admetus (cf. Verg. G. 3, 2); acc. to Cic. N. D. 3, 23, 57, it is from νόμος, lex, and denotes the fourth Apollo: “Paeanem aut Nomionem citārimus,” Cic. de Or. 1, 59, 251 Klotz.—
II. A son of Apollo and of Cyrene, the daughter of Hypseus, king of Thessaly, Just. 13, 7, 7.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
